title: Morning routine chart for school: visual schedule | ELUM
description: A morning routine chart for school days that means fewer "hurry up"s. How to set the order, what to do the night before, and action card examples.
keywords: morning routine chart, morning routine for school, school morning checklist, getting ready for school, morning routine for kids, visual morning routine
heading: Making a morning routine chart for school
lede: Mornings feel rushed not because there's so much to do, but because you have to decide what comes next every single time.

sections.heading: Set the order once
paragraphs: The morning routine is the same every day. Once you set the order and make it into cards, the cards tell your child what to do next, so you don't have to say each step.
list: Write the steps in the order you actually do them at home (wash → clothes → breakfast → bag)
Put steps that take a long time near the start
Make the last card a clear finish, like "go to the front door"

sections.heading: Get half of it done the night before
list: Lay out tomorrow's clothes in one place
Pack the bag ahead of time and leave it by the front door
Before bed, flip through tomorrow's routine cards together once

sections.heading: Using it in the morning
paragraphs: Keep the device in the same spot every day, and let your child check off each card when it's done. When your child stops, point to the card instead of hurrying them with words.
When everything is done, give the reward you chose right away. Since there's not much time before school, something short like one favorite song works well.

sections.heading: Rainy days and gym days
paragraphs: For days that are different from usual, make one more routine. In ELUM, write something like "get ready for school on a rainy day," and you get cards that include an umbrella and rain boots.

cards.title: Action card example: getting ready for school

items.title: Get dressed
items.body: Put on the clothes laid out

items.title: Eat breakfast
items.body: Sit at the table to eat

faq.q: Every morning, my child gets stuck on one step for a long time.
faq.a: Try splitting that step into two or three cards. If getting dressed is hard, make separate cards for the top, pants and socks.
You can make a separate weekend routine. Keeping the same steps, like washing up and getting dressed, helps the routine stay familiar.
